newsitem.title: FRANCE: Promodes sees 97 sales over 180 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Promodes sees 97 sales over 180 bln Ffr.

text.p: Promodes chairman Paul-Louis Halley said on Thursday he expected the French retailer's sales to be more than 180 billion francs in 1997 and between 230 and 240 billion in the year 2000.

Halley told a meeting with analysts and journalists that bearing in mind these figures "there is no reason to grow for the sake of growing or to carry out transactions which don't create value," Halley said.
Promodes sales were 168 billion francs in 1996.
"The priority is internal growth," he said.
He said there was no need for external growth except in Italy where he said the company was not large enough.
Halley also said he expected Promodes to invest four billion francs in 1997, up from three billion in 1996.
He said the group's priority was Europe, especially southern Europe, and it was also focusing on Asia and Latin America.

Promodes said sales excluding taxes in the first four months of 1997 were 33.4 billion francs, up 5.2 percent compared with the comparable period in 1996. On a like-for-like basis sales were up 6.7 percent.
